topics.label: Lecture introduction to complement
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the complement lecture, framing its importance and addressing its notoriously complex nomenclature.

topics.label: Foundational concepts and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational architecture, naming conventions, and central C3 reaction that anchor the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three pathways that initiate complement on pathogens and the concentration threshold required for activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of activated complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three primary effector outcomes of complement activation: opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory factors and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical presentations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how deficiencies in specific complement components produce distinct clinical diseases and susceptibility patterns.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, evolve diverse mechanisms to evade complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and next topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the complement lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
